Angiofibromas ( Figure 1 ) are benign fibroblastic tumors that histologically comprise bland spindle cells in a variably myxoid to collagenous stroma with a prominent vascular network. They present as telangiectatic, skin colored to pink to red-brown, dome-shaped papules with a glistening surface that primarily occur in the central part of the face, especially the nose. They may be mistaken for acne but do not spontaneously resolve. panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Panel A is a venous-phase CT image from a MEN1 case report showing the patient's pancreatic head mass, consistent with a pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor. B: Panel B is an arterial-phase CT image from the same MEN1 case report showing the patient's pancreatic head mass, consistent with a pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor. C: Panel C is a CT image from a MEN1 case report showing a right adrenal low-density nodule that was clinically interpreted as an adrenal adenoma. This is an associated finding in MEN1, but the specific adrenal adenoma finding is not represented in the provided vocabulary, so it is captured as a proposed finding.
